title: Counterexamples to the Ramos conjecture for two hyperplanes
summary: For every $n\ge2$, we construct $4n-2$ nondegenerate Gaussian measures on $\mathbb{R}^{6n-3}$ that cannot be simultaneously equipartitioned by two affine hyperplanes. This disproves the Ramos conjecture for two hyperplanes. Combined with known upper bounds, the construction shows that $3\cdot2^{s-1}-2$ is the least dimension guaranteeing a common two-hyperplane equipartition of $2^s-2$ absolutely continuous probability measures, for every $s\ge3$.
